title: The Poverty of Judas and the Fate of the Rich
english: Was he more wretched than Judas Iscariot? And he gained nothing from his poverty toward salvation, but while dining with the eleven poor ones and with the philosophers, and even with the Lord himself, who through us became voluntarily poor, he was driven there by a bad intention toward the love of money, and from there he contrived the betrayal.

It is also worthy to test the departure of another of the dead. For the poor man, having fallen asleep, had angels as guards and attendants, leading him with good hope to the place of rest; but the rich man, having died, is said to have been buried (Luke 16:22). For there is nothing like using that scriptural word, which through a single word sufficiently interprets the dishonorable dissolution of the rich.

For the sinner finishing his life is truly being buried, the body being earthly and of the soil, and the soul, having drawn its nature toward the flesh's longing for matter, leaving behind no useful memorial of his own life, and being covered shamefully and finishing the death of the pastures. For the body has a tomb, but the soul has Hades; two dark prisons being divided for the punishment of the evil creature.
